# local 0019: mcs51: volatile struct members and array elements in near data are read once for each use of the value

- Category: [Fixes that need a decision](../../fix-decision.md)
- Evidence: tested on r17228
- Recommended action: Apply the patch. Confirm its test of the declared type, which keeps pseudo symbols for unions. ds390 and pic16 were not built.
- Patch: [local-0019.patch](../../patches/local-0019.patch), commit [`8ce0a3bf8`](https://github.com/mdmower/sdcc/commit/8ce0a3bf815329ff72f5a0dcf87e05379cbfd628). Applies to r17228 without the other patches.
<!-- end of generated block -->

## Finding

On r17228, each function below reads its volatile object twice, and the source reads it once.

```c
struct s { unsigned char c; volatile unsigned char m; };
__data struct s st;
__data volatile unsigned char a[4];
unsigned char g, h;

void member (void) { unsigned char x = st.m; g = x; h = x; }
void element (void) { unsigned char x = a[1]; g = x; h = x; }
```

`sdcc -mmcs51 -S ps.c` gives `mov _g,(_st + 0x0001)`, `mov _h,(_st + 0x0001)` for `member()`, and
`mov _g,(_a + 0x0001)`, `mov _h,(_a + 0x0001)` for `element()`. With `--model-large`, `member()`
is `mov dptr,#_g`, `mov a,(_st + 0x0001)`, `movx @dptr,a`, `mov dptr,#_h`, `mov a,(_st + 0x0001)`,
`movx @dptr,a`, and `element()` has the same six instructions with `_a`.

The code reads the object where it uses the value. With the small model, `x = st.m; w = 1; g = x;`
with a volatile `w` writes `w` and then reads `st.m`. Members of 16 and 32 bits, members of a
volatile struct or union, and members of a volatile struct inside a struct are read once for each
use too. So is each member of a struct in `__data` with `__at`, because `checkSClass()` in
`src/SDCCsymt.c` makes every object with `__at` volatile. Members of structs in `__idata` and in
`__xdata` are read once, and so is a `__data volatile unsigned char` outside a struct or an
array. With `--model-large`, a struct without a storage class is in xdata, so the fault needs
`__data` in the declaration.

The values were also observed in uCsim, with `st` at `__data __at (0x60)` and the simulator
interface at address 0x61 of internal RAM, which is `st.m`. The interface returns the next byte
of an answer for each read, and the answer begins with 2, 1, and 4. After
`x = st.m; g = x; h = x;` with the small model, `g` is 2 and `h` is 1. With `--model-large`, a
statement `result[3] = g;` that follows them reads `st.m` a third time and stores 4.

## Cause

`regTypeNum()` in `src/mcs51/ralloc.c` converts an iTemp to a pseudo symbol when the one
definition of the iTemp is a read through a near pointer and `ptrPseudoSymSafe()` in
`src/SDCCptropt.c` returns 1. `ptrPseudoSymConvert()` then gives the iTemp the address expression
of the object as its spill location, so each use of the iTemp is a direct access to the object.
`ptrPseudoSymSafe()` tests the live range of the iTemp for calls and for writes through pointers,
and it does not test whether the object is volatile. The function is from
[r3297](https://sourceforge.net/p/sdcc/code/3297/). `regTypeNum()` of ds390 and of pic16 calls it
too, and the call in `src/pic14/ralloc.c` is inside `#if 0`.

## Fix

`ptrPseudoSymSafe()` returns 0 when two conditions hold. The type that the pointer of the read
points to is volatile, and the new function `declaredVolatile()` finds `volatile` in the type of
the base symbol, for the object, for its elements, or for a member at any depth. The code then
reads the object once, where the source reads it.

## Decision

- The second condition is there for unions. `geniCodeStruct()` sets the volatile flag in the
  iCode type of each member of every union
  ([r16953](https://sourceforge.net/p/sdcc/code/16953/), bug #4072). With the first condition
  alone, which is one test without `declaredVolatile()`, the files `frexpf.c`, `ldexpf.c`, and
  `printf_large.c` of the mcs51-small library compile to longer code. Each has a union in near
  data that is not declared volatile. With both conditions, the three files compile to the code
  that they have without the patch.
- With both conditions, the read of a union member that is not declared volatile is not converted
  when the type of the base symbol has a volatile declaration for another member. The code for
  that read is correct and longer than it needs to be. Reads through a cast to a volatile type do
  not need the second condition, because `ptrPseudoSymSafe()` returns 0 for every cast in the
  rematerialization of the pointer.
- For mcs51-small, the code of the regression suite is 312 bytes larger with the patch, in 8
  tests, and `gi = st.m` with an `unsigned int gi` has one more instruction. A condition on
  `st.m`, `g = st.m`, and `g = st.m + 1` compile to the code that they have without the patch.
- ds390 and pic16 were not built.

## Verification

`support/regression/tests/volatile-aggregate-read.c` has 22 assertions. Six helper functions read
a volatile object once, use the value twice, and change the object between the uses. The objects
are struct members of 8 and 16 bits, an array element, a member of a volatile struct, a member of
a volatile struct inside a struct, and a volatile member of a union. Two more functions use the
value once, after the object has changed. For mcs51, an instruction in inline assembly changes
the object, because a write in C to the object prevents the pseudo symbol.

On r17228, 8 of the 22 assertions fail for mcs51-small and mcs51-large, one for each helper
function. With earlier patches of this report, 8 fail for each of the six mcs51 variants, which
are the four models and `--stack-auto` with the small and large models. With the patch, the test
passes on these six, host, stm8, and ucz80.

Two programs that are not part of the patch count reads in uCsim with the interface of Finding,
for objects at absolute addresses and for a struct member that the linker places. Without the
patch, 5 of the 8 functions of the first program and 3 of the 6 of the second read the object
more than once with the small model, and 6 and 4 with the other three models. The source of each
has one read. With the patch, each of these functions reads the object once for the six variants.

With the patches of this report, the regression suite has 0 failures for host, mcs51-small,
mcs51-medium, mcs51-large, mcs51-huge, mcs51-small-stack-auto, mcs51-large-stack-auto, stm8, and
ucz80, and the diagnostics suite has 0 failures for mcs51, mcs51-large, mcs51-stack-auto, z80,
and stm8.

For mcs51-small, the assembly of six other tests differs: `gte/930930-2.c`, `bug-2448.c`,
`bug-4255.c`, `critical.c`, `gcc-torture-execute-20001228-1.c`, and `oldfmul.c`. Each has a
volatile union, struct, or array in near data. The assembly of the tests that are made from
`.c.in` templates was not compared. For mcs51-large, the code of every test has the size that it
has without the patch. For mcs51-huge, `cse.c` is 1 byte larger. The argument of one of its calls
is a member of a struct in `__data` that is declared with `__at`, and `checkSClass()` gives
objects with an absolute address a volatile type. Of the library assembly files, `__fs2ulonglong.asm` and
`__ulonglong2fs.asm` of mcs51-small differ, and their sources declare a
`volatile union float_long`. The library files of the other five mcs51 models, stm8, stm8-large,
and z80 are identical with and without the patch.

## Related

- The entry local 0014 is about a volatile right operand of an assignment that is read again for
  each use of the value of the assignment. With its patch and without this one, `g = w = st.m`
  with a volatile `w` reads `st.m` twice.
- A fault with objects that are not volatile was found on r17228, with the small and the large
  model. `x = nst.m; *dp = 5; g = x;` leaves 5 in `g` when `dp` points to `g`.
  `packRegsForAssign()` in `src/mcs51/ralloc.c` makes `g` the result of the read, and its search
  does not stop at a write through a pointer that can point to `g`. The code stores to `g`
  before the write through `dp`.
- A second fault with objects that are not volatile is present with and without the patch. When
  the `__idata` pointer `ip` points to `nst.m`, `x = nst.m; *ip = 5; g = x; h = x;` stores 5 in
  `g` and `h`.
  `ptrPseudoSymSafe()` treats a write through a pointer that is not a near or a generic pointer
  as a write to another memory space, and an `__idata` pointer can point to an object in `__data`.
